content.title: HBO’s ‘Harry Potter’ Teaser Reveals Draco, Dumbledore, Snape, the Dursleys, and More. Here’s Everything We Know
content.text: Along with the first footage from the all-new Harry Potter adaptation, the teaser gives us the show's official title—and a surprise release date.Aidan Monaghan/Courtesy of HBOThe first teaser trailer for HBO's Harry Potter series has arrived, bringing with it new images of the Harry Potter cast in character—and a reveal of the show's official title and release date. Read on for everything we currently know about the year's most anticipated TV reboot.It's been almost a decade and a half since The Deathly Hallows Pt. II, which is a pretty long time to go without a reboot for a franchise as huge as Harry Potter, not least in the age of rapacious IP exploitation. Yeah, sure, the Fantastic Beasts movies scratched an itch for the wannabe wizards of the world, and the triple-A video game Hogwarts Legacy provided a veritable Floo Network for millions of Potterheads. But neither holds a magically floating candle to the O.G. films, right?So now comes an HBO Harry Potter TV series adapting the original Harry Potter novels, which is expected to be epic in length, rolling out over the course of a decade (or more).This week HBO released the logline for the first season, which (in case you're somehow unfamiliar with the story of this literary and cinematic mega-franchise) reads as follows:“There is nothing special about Harry Potter—at least that's what his Aunt Petunia always says. On his 11th birthday, a letter of admittance to Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry opens up a hidden world for Harry: one of fun, friendship and magic. But with this new adventure comes great risk as Harry is forced to face a dangerous enemy from his past.”Aidan Monaghan/HBOThe film series made stars of Daniel Radcliffe, Emma Watson and Rupert Grint, and introduced a new generation of fans to beloved British and Irish character actors like Alan Rickman, Michael Gambon, Gary Oldman, Robbie Coltrane, and Imelda Staunton. HBO’s Harry Potter has become the hottest casting target for British talent this side of Game of Thrones, even if enthusiasm for the project has been dampened by Potter creator J.K. Rowling's ongoing social-media crusade against trans rights. (HBO head Casey Bloys has described Rowling as “fairly involved” with the series’ development, while noting that her presence hasn't put anyone off signing up, per IndieWire.)Nevertheless, all involved have a formidable challenge on their hands. Can they live up to the beloved character portrayals that gave the movies their magic? We'll find out when the first season—officially entitled Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone—hits HBO this Christmas. In the meantime, check out the first official teaser for the HBO Harry Potter's first season.Below, we run down the Harry Potter cast as presently constituted, and speculate on a few key roles that have yet to be cast.Confirmed castHarry, Ron and HermioneDominic McLaughlin as Harry PotterAidan Monaghan/Courtesy of HBOAs expected, all three actors playing the young principals in HBO's Harry Potter series—Dominic McLaughlin (Harry Potter), Arabella Stanton (Hermione Granger), and Alastair Stout (Ron Weasley)—are screen newcomers. When we say “newcomers," we mean it—of the three, McLaughlin is the only one with an IMDb page (which aside from Potter, lists only one other acting credit, in an upcoming Sky original movie about an ill-tempered pumpkin farmer.)Arabella Stanton as Hermione GrangerAidan Monaghan/Courtesy of HBO“After an extraordinary search led by casting directors Lucy Bevan and Emily Brockmann, we are delighted to announce we have found our Harry, Hermione, and Ron," showrunner Francesca Gardiner and director Mark Mylod said in a statement. "The talent of these three unique actors is wonderful to behold, and we cannot wait for the world to witness their magic together onscreen. We would like to thank all the tens of thousands of children who auditioned. It's been a real pleasure to discover the plethora of young talent out there.”Alastair Stout as Ron WeasleyAidan Monaghan/Courtesy of HBODumbledoreJohn Lithgow as DumbledoreCourtesy of HBOFollowing months of speculation, HBO finally confirmed last year that it'll be veteran actor John Lithgow as Dumbledore. Casting an American in Potter's second biggest role might come with its own dose of controversy for British fans, but lay down the torches for a moment. Nailing the British accent is nothing to an actor of Lithgow's caliber (recall his turn as Winston Churchill in The Crown), and perhaps it's only fair that an American should take the role of one of modern fiction's most famous Englishmen for once, given how Britain's acting exports disproportionately dominate the small screen across the Atlantic. Besides which, Lithgow's many Emmys and Oscar nominations speak for themselves.In a March interview with The New York Times, Lithgow revealed that the social-media outrage around the Harry Potter series and its connection to Rowling prompted him to consider walking away from the show. He told the Times that while he doesn't agree with Rowling's views on transgender issues, he sees the material itself as “clearly on the side of the angels, against intolerance and bigotry,” and decided to stick with the project despite the fact that “[in] every interview I will ever do for the rest of my life this will come up.”SnapePaapa Essiedu as SnapeCourtesy of HBOI May Destroy You and The Lazarus Project's Paapa Essiedu has been officially announced as the next Snape. His star has rapidly risen in recent years, with roles in Gangs of London, Saoirse Ronan's film The Outrun, and a standout turn in Black Mirror serving to cement his screen bonafides. Expect his Harry Potter part to shoot him into the A-list stratosphere—and we have no doubt he'll match up to the might of Alan Rickman.HagridAidan Monaghan/Courtesy of HBOActor/comedian Nick Frost, a mainstay of Edgar Wright's Cornetto Trilogy, is confirmed for Hagrid. It's the perfect marriage of role and actor, as far as we're concerned: Hogwarts' very own BFG will allow Frost to play a less immediately comic part than we'd usually associate him with, while his own comedic instincts will surely bring out Hagrid's funnier side. At one point, Ted Lasso's Brett Goldstein was reportedly up for the role—which would have been a very different direction indeed.HBO released the first behind-the-scenes shot of Frost in Hagrid garb on July 15, and yep, he sure looks like a gigantic, beardy wizard. (Frost has since been papped in costume while filming scenes for the Harry Potter revival with McLaughlin on the streets of London.) Frost's frequent collaborator Edgar Wright, who gave the actor his big break with TV show Spaced (and most famously directed him in the Cornetto film trilogy), had a short and simple response on Instagram: “I would. #shagrid”Professor Filius FlitwickAidan Monaghan/Courtesy of HBOHBO's Harry Potter has its first returning cast member in the form of Warwick Davis, who will play the role that he originated in the films: Professor Filius Flitwick. The eccentric goblin-wizard master of charms at Hogwarts, Davis' Flitwick is as memorable for his lovable personality as he is for his big moustache (though he first appeared much older, with a bushy grey beard), and was present throughout the movies right up to the Battle of Hogwarts in The Deathly Hallows, Part II.We're yet to have word as to whether Davis' casting is a one-off, or if the production intends to cast more cast members from the film series for the show. Nonetheless, we now know that return castings are on the table—and who'd write off a cameo or two?Garrick OllivanderAnton Lesser HBO veteran Anton Lesser, known to Game of Thrones fans as the disgraced ex-maester-turned-necromancer Qyburn, will take on the role of Diagon Alley's master wandmaker, a part originated onscreen by the late British acting legend John Hurt. Lesser's other credits include Wolf Hall, two seasons as UK Prime Minister Harold MacMillan on The Crown, and his recent stint as Major Partagaz on Disney+'s Andor.Neville LongbottomRory Wilmot Rory Wilmot, who'll also be seen in the upcoming Netflix miniseries Out of the Dust, has been cast as Harry's Gryffindor classmate Neville Longbottom, a part originated by Matthew Lewis in the theatrical films.Rolanda HoochLouise Brealey Hogwarts' flying instructor and Quidditch referee Madam Hooch will be played by Louise Brealey, known for Hulu and A24's Such Brave Girls; Zoë Wanamaker played the character in Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone.Draco MalfoyLox Pratt as Draco MalfoyCourtesy of HBONewcomer Lox Pratt, most recently seen in the BBC/Netflix adaptation of Lord of the Flies, will play Draco Malfoy, Harry's arch rival, as originally portrayed by Tom Felton. He's got blond hair and blue eyes, so he certainly looks the part. Draco plays a significant role across both the films and books: a snooty kid with a real sour streak, he tries to befriend Harry early on, only to be snubbed for his less-than-savory traits (the fact that he calls Hermione a “mudblood,” all the bullying). From then on, as the figurehead of Slytherin house at Hogwarts, he embarks on a fierce rivalry with Harry, with the pair butting heads numerous times.Lucius MalfoyLONDON, ENGLAND - DECEMBER 18: Johnny Flynn attends the press night after party for "The Motive And The Cue" at Cafe At The Crypt, St-Martins-in-the-Field, on December 18, 2023 in London, England. (Photo by Matt Keeble/Dave Benett/Getty Images)Dave Benett/Getty ImagesFirst playing a significant role in Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets, Draco's nasty dad—who infamously abuses his house elf Dobby, and holds deep Nazi-wizard sympathies—will be portrayed by Johnny Flynn. He was originally played by Jason Isaacs in the films. No, we can't wait to see how the white wig looks.The DursleysPhotographed by Aidan Monaghan /A cornerstone of Harry's rise-from-the-ashes origin story is his neglectful upbringing under adoptive parents Petunia and Vernon Dursley. They'll be portrayed by The Diary of a Teenage Girl's Bel Powley and Flowers' Daniel Rigby, who take over from Fiona Shaw and Richard Griffiths; newcomer Amos Kitson will play Harry's occasional tormentor Dudley Dursley.Amos Kitson as Dudley DursleyAidan Monaghan/Courtesy of HBOMolly WeasleyBy taking on the role of Ron's zany mom, English actress and comedian Katherine Parkinson has an unenviable task on her hands. Who would want to follow such a totemic acting force as Julie Waters? But we back the Rivals and IT Crowd star to shine as Potter's beloved maternal figure—there's little reason to doubt she'll nail the salt-of-the-earth charm that made Molly such a fan favorite.Cornelius FudgeDave Benett/Getty ImagesThe Crown saw Bertie Carvel join the long lineage of actors to play the UK's Prime Minister with his take on Tony Blair, so it's only fitting that he'll now slip into the shoes of the Minister of Magic. Played by Robert Hardy in the original films, it is Fudge's lackluster leadership—and unfounded paranoia that he will be overthrown by Dumbledore and his allies—that helps bring about the return of Voldemort. Hardy played Fudge in four films.McGonagallJanet McTeer as McGonagallCourtesy of HBOIt'll be Janet McTeer of Albert Nobbs, Ozark and The Menu as McGonagall, the Hogwarts matriarch played by the late, great Maggie Smith in the films. Smith is another tough example to live up to, but McTeer certainly has the talent and look.Professor Quirrell and FilchScreen newcomer Luke Thallon, a 29-year-old actor fresh off his acclaimed run as Hamlet for the Royal Shakespeare Company, has been cast as Professor Quirrell. Notably, it's his first major screen credit; could we see him take the reigns as Voldemort later down the line, too?Another astute casting comes in the form of British comedy legend Paul Whitehouse as Filch. The Fast Show star might be a surprising pick for Filch, Hogwart's ill-tempered muggle cleaner, but maybe that's the point—HBO appears to be leaning into comedy with this Harry Potter cast, and Whitehouse might help file off Filch's rough edges.SpeculationTom Felton as… who?Justin Tallis/Getty ImagesTake this one with a real pinch of salt, but the Daily Mail has reported that O.G. Draco Malfoy actor Tom Felton—who returned to the part of Draco last year in the Broadway production of Harry Potter and the Cursed Child—is being considered by HBO and J.K. Rowling for involvement in the reboot series. While the article notes long-standing fan interest in seeing Felton return as Draco's father Lucius, who was portrayed by Jason Isaacs in the movies, the author suggests that “this is unlikely,” because “the showrunners want to use him in other ways.”The Mail's source is quoted as saying that, rather than being part of the primary cast, Felton could be deployed in a number of ways behind the scenes. “There has even been talk of getting him involved in creating behind-the-scenes content for HBO which could form part of a documentary about the making of the TV show,” the source said. How else could he appear? Fans on Reddit suggest that he could make for a good narrator, for one, and don't write off a background appearance.VoldemortPaul Bettany at the 53rd Annual Saturn Awards held at Universal Hilton on March 08, 2026 in Los Angeles, California. (Photo by JC Olivera/Variety via Getty Images)JC Olivera/Getty ImagesYou need a serpentine, slippery fellow for He Who Must Not Be Named—the sort of actor whose very presence can feel terrifying. (It also helps if you can picture them taking on the look of Munch’s The Scream after a few hours of prosthetics and make-up.) We still have no official word on who'll play the Harry Potter series’ ultimate Big Bad in the HBO show, but the latest actor to deny that he's playing the part (despite rumors to the contrary) is Paul Bettany, the MCU's Vision. “I haven't heard anything about that,” he told ScreenRant at the Saturn Awards in March. "I’m a big fan of the IP, and I’m a big fan of HBO, but nobody has called me up about that.”For a younger pick, we'd suggest the HBO Potter bosses look no further than Stranger Things’ Jamie Campbell Bower, whose villainous Vecna is as gross and spine-chillingly malignant as you’d ever want Voldemort to be. He did play the young version of another evil wizard, Grindelwald, in the Potter film universe. But does that really matter?Sirius BlackKit Harington. He's unhinged, erratic, and just a little bit disheveled—but, crucially, kind of endearing. The Sirius Black formula is a tough one to crack. Do you go the Gary Oldman route and recruit an actor you can reliably expect to perform to the back of the hall, or go for someone who will offer a subtler approach to Black's inner turmoil? Either way, Kit Harington would be our first choice: he's a range-y performer who fits the age profile, can play to both Black's light and shade, and he just seems like he'd be a cool godfather. A word here, too, for fellow Game of Thrones alumnus Richard Madden, who carries many of the same qualities, though we'd expect a more introspective version of Black from him.Some fringe shouts could be Benedict Cumberbatch, although he's on the upper end of the likely age range. And could fellow MCU actor Tom Hiddleston inject Black with a little of Loki's mania? He certainly seems the right fit from the A-list Hollywood crop—and it's worth noting that, at 43, he's around the same age as Oldman when he shot Prisoner of Azkaban, give or take a few years.Bellatrix LestrangeMia Goth. The way that we imagine Bellatrix is so specific to Helena Bonham Carter that it'll be an uphill battle for anyone who is called upon to bring their own interpretation to the role—but such is the case for most of this cast. To our mind, the standout nominee would be Mia Goth, the scream queen whose turn in 2022's Pearl was considered Oscar-worthy enough for commentators to question why another performance in a horror film had been snubbed after she missed out on a nomination. Her knack for playing women on the edge would serve Bellatrix well.This story originally appeared in British GQ.Killian Faith-Kelly is a writer from County Derry who now lives in London. He writes mostly for GQ, mostly about culture. He's also written for The Fence, New Critique, the Press Gazette and the Radio Times, and has been described as “very talented” by such critics as his mum. You ...
